newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says will cut VAT on fuel.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says will cut VAT on fuel.

text.p: A UK Labour government would cut the level of Value Added Tax levied on fuel prices, Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Wednesday.
Brown said Labour would cut VAT on fuel from eight percent to five -- its first manifesto pledge to cut taxes.
"The reason I'm doing it now is that I think the Chancellor should include it in his budget," Brown told BBC radio.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will unveil his budget on November 26.
"It is a matter of principle for us that it should never have been introduced," Brown said.
"VAT on fuel has discouraged many pensioners from turning up their heating when they should do so," Brown said.
He said five percent was the minimum level that VAT could be reduced to and said Clarke could do it within his existing resources.
"I personally would prefer to...abolish it altogether but that cannot be done," Brown said.
The tax, once introduced, can only be cut to five percent because of European Union rules.
Brown refused to be drawn on what Labour would do with income tax.
"One of the main complaints I have of the Chancellor is that he is unprepared to tell us what the true state of the public finances is," Brown said.
"We will make our decision about tax rates having reviewed and made our assessment of the state of the economy, after the budget and in time for that to be included in our manifesto."
Clarke will be unable to show his hand and comment on policy specifics ahead of the budget.
